questions.q: What are the three production databases at Meridian Fleet Logistics, and what is each one's core problem?
options: There is only one database, split across three servers
OrderManagement, DriverHR, and Telemetry are all identical copies of the same sales database
The three databases are HR, Payroll, and Marketing
OrderManagement (dispatch timeouts 7-9am), DriverHR (unaudited access to sensitive SSN/license data), and Telemetry (fast-growing storage from GPS feeds)
questions.explain: Each database has a distinct, specific problem — this project treats them as three separate decisions, not one blanket fix.

questions.q: Why does this lesson describe the business requirements as stakeholder quotes rather than a to-do list?
options: Because quotes are easier to read than bullet points
Because real DBA work starts from a stated situation and constraint, not a pre-solved technical checklist — translating it into decisions is the actual job
Because the stakeholders don't actually know what they want
Because a to-do list would have been more accurate and this lesson just chose a different style for fun
questions.explain: The CFO, Ops Director, Compliance Officer, and CEO each describe a situation in their own words — turning that into deployment, security, performance, and HA/DR decisions is exactly what Lessons 91-93 do.

questions.q: The Compliance Officer's concern in this lesson points most directly toward which later decision?
options: The performance tuning decision in Lesson 92
No later lesson addresses this concern
The disaster recovery architecture decision in Lesson 93
The security controls decision in Lesson 91 — authentication, encryption, and access for the DriverHR database's sensitive columns
questions.explain: An unaudited shared login on a table with SSNs and license numbers is a security/access problem, which Lesson 91 addresses using Chapters 4-6's concepts.

questions.q: The CEO's request to know 'exactly how bad an outage would be, in hours and minutes' is a request for what two specific numbers, introduced formally in Lesson 93?
options: RTO (Recovery Time Objective) and RPO (Recovery Point Objective)
CPU and memory utilization percentages
Backup file size and compression ratio
DTU and vCore
questions.explain: "How long until we're back up" is RTO; "how much data could we lose" is RPO — Lesson 93 has the CEO state these as concrete numbers and asks you to derive the right architecture from them.

questions.q: Why does this chapter treat Lessons 90-93 as one continuous scenario instead of four separate, unrelated exercises?
options: Because it saves the author time to reuse the same company name
Because DP-300 requires exactly four lessons per chapter

Because a real production environment doesn't have isolated problems — the same databases, constraints, and stakeholders carry through migration, security, performance, automation, and disaster recovery decisions together
Because the four lessons are actually unrelated and the shared setup is coincidental
questions.explain: Meridian Fleet Logistics is the same environment throughout — the deployment choice in Lesson 91 shapes the automation options in Lesson 92 and the HA/DR architecture in Lesson 93.
